“Snow cover” refers to the amount of land covered by snow at any given time. As EPA’s Snow Cover indicator explains, snow cover is important for many plants and animals, and people and ecosystems also rely on snowmelt to replenish streams and groundwater. As temperature and precipitation patterns change, so can the overall area covered by snow. However, snow cover is not just something that is affected by climate change. It also exerts an influence on climate, because light-colored snow reflects most of the sunlight that hits it, unlike darker surfaces that absorb more energy and heat up more quickly. Thus, more snow cover means more energy is reflected back into space, resulting in cooling, while less snow cover means more energy is absorbed at the Earth’s surface, resulting in warming.
